questions: When a die is rolled, does each face have equal probability of appearing, i.e., are the dice fair?
Are the numbers on a die's faces guaranteed to be distinct, or can the same number appear on multiple faces of the same die?
If a die has duplicate numbers on its faces, should the probability of rolling a particular number be counted proportionally to its frequency on that die?
When choosing the two dice "optimally," are we allowed to choose the same die twice (i.e., roll the same die two times) or must the two dice be distinct?
If the two dice must be distinct, does the order of selection matter for the probability calculation, or is the pair considered unordered?
Should the output be printed as a decimal number, a fraction, or is any format acceptable as long as the numeric value meets the error tolerance?
Are there any constraints on the size of the numbers A_{i,j} beyond the given range that could cause overflow, and how should such cases be handled in the computation?
In the case where multiple pairs of dice achieve the same maximal probability, does it matter which pair is considered, or is only the maximal probability value required?
answers: Yes — each die is fair; every face is equally likely when rolled.

inline_prompts:
There are N dice.  
The i-th die has K_i faces, with the numbers A_{i,1}, A_{i,2}, \ldots, A_{i,K_i} written on them.  
When you roll this die, each face appears with equal probability.  
You choose two dice from the N dice and roll them.  
Determine the probability that the two dice show the same number, when the dice are chosen optimally.  
Input  
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:  
N  
K_1 A_{1,1} A_{1,2} \dots A_{1,K_1}  
\vdots  
K_N A_{N,1} A_{N,2} \dots A_{N,K_N}  
Output  
Print the answer.  
Your answer is considered correct if the absolute or relative error from the true solution does not exceed 10^{-8}.  
Constraints  
- 2 \leq N \leq 100  
- 1 \leq K_i  
- K_1 + K_2 + \dots + K_N \leq 10^5  
- 1 \leq A_{i,j} \leq 10^5  
- All input values are integers.
